title: Searching a layered graph
sub: Approximate nearest-neighbour search the way HNSW does it, on 300 points in 2-D.

frames.caption: 300 vectors, each linked to its nearest neighbours. HNSW stacks layers: every vector is on layer 0, about a quarter also on layer 1, a sixteenth on layer 2. Search starts at the top: only 13 nodes, so the links are long. The query is red.
Greedy search on the top layer: hop to whichever neighbour is closer to the query, until none is. A few long hops cross most of the space.
Drop to layer 1 at the same node and repeat with denser, shorter links.

Layer 0 has every vector. A last few short hops reach the nearest neighbour (the same one brute force finds), after computing 38 distances instead of 300. With millions of vectors the saving is enormous, because the number of hops grows roughly like log N. The answer is approximate in general: greedy search can stop at a local optimum, which is why HNSW keeps a list of ef candidates rather than just one.
